title: the brigade is not cleaned before the backend connection goes back to the pool
live_proof: this corpus pins the allocators (APR 1.7.4, apr-util 1.6.3), not httpd; a case reproduces the call sequence rather than a shipped tree, and says so instead of asserting liveness
object: nodes from the connection's bucket allocator, still named by the brigade
lifetime_ender: the connection, and with it the allocator, being handed to the next request
shape: a recycled allocator serving its next user
allocator_layer: apr_bucket_alloc_t over apr_pool_t over apr_allocator_t -- two recycling levels, neither reaching malloc
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocators: apr_buckets_alloc.c and apr_pools.c are upstream byte for byte through the port's shims; brigades, filters, connections and requests are reduced to the holder and the storage

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm leaves storage named after its owner gave it back; the fixed arm does not
native-fix-differential.note: this pair differs by whether the upstream fix is applied, not by protection
native-fix-differential.measures: free() is interposed and counted, so freed_to_malloc is measured per case and not inherited from the census

native-detect.requires: neither level reaches malloc, so ASan has no event; Valgrind against APR's own annotations is the arm that could discriminate

status: native pair run 2026-09-21; both passed. No protected arm exists: the allocators build freestanding but no domain workload does
note: the protected arms are unwritten because the port is a census plus this corpus, not a domain workload. The gap is declared rather than absent
